messages.subject: Conditional Panel Issue (Newbie)
parts:
Hi,
I am uploading 2 files, into tabsets. I am able to do this fine.
After uploading (that is conditional on successful uploading), I need to be able to present the file headers back in a group check box.
This is where I am having trouble. In the code below, I am I am reading in dsdFile, rendering it as table dsdTable, and attempting to make checkboxes from names(dsdTable).

I do not have any success in getting the check boxes to show on successful upload.
What am I doing wrong?
Thanks
Simson

ui

library(shiny)

shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(
  headerPanel("Randomization"),
  sidebarPanel(
    fileInput('dsdFile', 'Disease Status', accept=c('text/csv', 'text/comma-separated-values,text/plain')),
    fileInput('nsdFile', 'Normal Status', accept=c('text/csv', 'text/comma-separated-values,text/plain')),
    tags$hr(),
uiOutput("dsdCheckBoxes")
  ),

  #mainPanel(    tableOutput('contents')  )

mainPanel
(
tabsetPanel
(
tabPanel("Disease Status", tableOutput("dsdData")),
tabPanel("Normal Status", tableOutput("nsdData"))
)
)

))


server

library(shiny)

shinyServer(function(input, output) 
{

  dsdData <- renderTable({

    dsdFile <- input$dsdFile

    if (is.null(dsdFile))
      return(NULL)
    
    read.csv(dsdFile$datapath)

  })

  nsdData <- renderTable({

    nsdFile <- input$nsdFile

    if (is.null(nsdFile))
      return(NULL)
    
    read.csv(nsdFile$datapath)

  })

  output$dsdCheckBoxes<- renderUI({

    if (is.null(dsdFile)) return(NULL)

    dsdCheckBoxes<- names(dsdData)

    checkboxGroupInput("dsdCheckBoxes", "Choose Variables", dsdCheckBoxes)

  })


output$dsdData <- dsdData 

output$nsdData <- nsdData 

})

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Conditional Panel Issue (Newbie)
parts:
1) You can't read dsdData and nsdData as if they are data frames. The return value from renderTable isn't a data frame; it's a value that is only useful for assigning to output$whatever. So if you want to access the data and use it from two or more places, you want to extract that part of the code and put it in a reactive expression. (Similar to how, in non-reactive code, you'd assign a variable.) Then you can access the value of that reactive expression from any other render or reactive code, by calling it as if it's a function. Like so:

dsdData <- reactive({
  # blah blah
  read.csv(dsdFile$datapath)
})

output$dsdData <- renderTable({ dsdData() })

output$dsdCheckBoxes <- renderUI({
  data <- dsdData()
  if (is.null(data)) return(NULL)
  dsdCheckBoxes <- names(data)
